display_name: The Fair Trading Act 1986 (NZ) under one top-level goal — for a piece of conduct, does it contravene the Act, is it an offence and up to what fine, is it an infringement offence, may a party seek a s 43 order and by when — and four goals: conduct, consumer transactions and auctions, information and safety, enforcement

others: the term may be declared unfair, … (fta-conduct.l4)
the refund on cancelling the layby (fta-transactions.l4)
is an uninvited direct sale agreement (fta-transactions.l4)
the gift card expiry date, sold … (fta-transactions.l4)
who may make a s 43 order of … (fta-enforcement.l4)

scope: Every provision of the Act as in the PCO's version as at 1 July 2026, from the text converted from the PCO XML, at the level its rules can be computed: which provision conduct contravenes and with what consequence, and every rule with a number, date or period. Inputs: the quality of the conduct (misleading, unconscionable, false, and so on); which weekdays are not working days; standards, notices and standard-form status; amounts fixed by other Acts. Carried as text: the provisions in `provisions carried as text`.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the Act. An independent test pass was run on 2026-10-15 (tests-independent.l4, 239 assertions from expectations written before the encoding was read). It found 2 disagreements, both resolved in its favour (s 32 needs trade; s 19(2) does not), and 4 gaps now closed (s 36V(2)(a), s 36Q, s 21A(2), s 31(2) scope). 239/239 now pass. The pipeline has not been run. On 2026-10-17, at the user's direction, Legislation Act 2019 s 55 was applied to the 3-year limit for applying for orders under s 43 (s 43A); the deadlines already counted in working days (ss 31A, 36Q-36R, 36ZF) end on working days; 1 independent assertion(s) written before that change now fail by design.

forks.F2: ss 36M, 36V: up to and including the 5th working day after receipt.
forks.F3: s 36ZF: the earlier of 10 working days after the sale and 5 after a request.
